analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר. The words הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לָכֶם (“Look, I have given you”) begin God's direct speech.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular וַיֹּאמֶר (“he said”). The speaker uses the first-person singular נָתַתִּי (“I have given”) to describe giving plants and fruit trees for food.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular agreement

analysis.evidence: In הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לָכֶם, “See, I have given you,” God draws the hearers’ attention to his gift of plants and fruit trees for food.
analysis.morphology: Presentative interjection, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: see now (a fact put before the hearer)

analysis.evidence: God is the speaker. לָכֶם identifies the recipients, and אֶת and וְאֶת introduce the seed-bearing plants and fruit trees as what God gives. לָכֶם יִהְיֶה לְאָכְלָה specifies their use as food.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular, with subject ending ־תִּי.
analysis.sense: give something to someone for their use

analysis.evidence: In נָתַתִּי לָכֶם אֶת כָּל עֵשֶׂב, לָכֶם identifies the recipients (“to you”), and אֶת introduces what God gives (“every plant”). The parallel וְאֶת כָּל הָעֵץ introduces the second object (“and every tree”).
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע, כָּל quantifies the singular noun עֵשֶׂב. The gift includes every plant that bears seed.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: כָּל עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע means “every seed-bearing plant.” The masculine singular participle זֹרֵעַ modifies עֵשֶׂב. The verse lists these plants alongside fruit trees as food.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: זֹרֵעַ modifies the masculine singular noun עֵשֶׂב ‘plant’ and takes זֶרַע ‘seed’ as its object. The phrase כָּל עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע means ‘every plant that bears seed’.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute

analysis.evidence: In עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע, “a plant yielding seed,” זֶרַע is the direct object of זֹרֵעַ and names what the plant produces.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying כָּל עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע, “every seed-bearing plant.” The clause עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ gives its location, “on the face of the whole earth,” with “is” understood.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, עַל locates the seed-bearing plants on the surface of the whole earth. Its complement פְּנֵי supplies the meaning “face” or “surface.”
analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, פְּנֵי is in construct with כָל הָאָרֶץ. The phrase locates the seed-bearing plants on the surface of the whole earth.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, both genders, plural construct.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, “on the face of the whole earth,” כָל takes the definite singular הָאָרֶץ as its complement and refers to the earth in its entirety.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ, “across the face of the whole earth,” פְּנֵי supplies the sense of surface, while כָל הָאָרֶץ names the whole earth over which the seed-bearing plants grow.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הָ־.

draft.change: Add Gen.1.29 as verse evidence for the existing אֵת … וְאֵת construction in the particle entry.
draft.definition: Marks a definite noun phrase as the direct object of a verb.
draft.evidence: In Gen.1.29, וְאֶת כָּל הָעֵץ introduces the second object of נָתַתִּי ‘I have given’, parallel to אֶת כָּל עֵשֶׂב.

analysis.evidence: נָתַתִּי לָכֶם means ‘I have given you’. The first אֶת introduces the plants given. At position 15, וְ joins כָּל הָעֵץ ‘every tree’ to that first gift, and אֶת marks the tree phrase as the second object of נָתַתִּי.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ ‘and’ + unsuffixed direct-object particle אֶת.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל הָעֵץ אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ פְרִי, the relative clause identifies which trees qualify. כָּל applies to each such tree, parallel to כָּל עֵשֶׂב earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל הָעֵץ means “every tree.” The relative clause אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ פְרִי describes the tree as bearing fruit.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying הָעֵץ “the tree.” The suffix on בּוֹ “in it” refers back to the tree, so אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ means “in which.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In פְרִי עֵץ, “fruit of a tree,” פְרִי stands in construct with עֵץ. The verse describes seed-bearing fruit and gives it as food.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In פְרִי עֵץ, “fruit of a tree,” פְרִי is the construct noun and עֵץ names the tree that bears the fruit.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In פְרִי עֵץ זֹרֵעַ זָרַע, the participle זֹרֵעַ takes זָרַע ‘seed’ as its object. The same construction occurs earlier in עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע ‘a plant bearing seed’.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: זֹרֵעַ זָרַע repeats the earlier phrase זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע, “yielding seed.” In both phrases the noun names what the plant produces. At the clause break, זֶרַע takes the pausal form זָרַע.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun in pausal form, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לָכֶם יִהְיֶה לְאָכְלָה, לָכֶם identifies the recipients and לְאָכְלָה states what the vegetation God has given them will serve as: food.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: After God gives the seed-bearing plants and fruit trees to the addressees, לָכֶם יִהְיֶה לְאָכְלָה states their intended use: “they shall serve as food for you.”
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition לְ plus a feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: food (what is given to be eaten)
